threads.body:
This test verifies `db.namespace` only on the span, but the new `db.client.operation.duration` dimension remains untested. Add the metric assertion with `DB_NAMESPACE`, as the Jedis and Lettuce database-index tests do, so dropping the namespace from metric attributes is caught.

This issue also appears on line 448 of the same file.

replies.body:
Addressed in d69e861fac89d4acf1ffb6654fd29201bbcac07d.

Analysis: Both `testNonDefaultDatabaseIndex` and `testNonDefaultDatabaseIndexTransaction` verified `DB_NAMESPACE` on the span but left the `db.client.operation.duration` metric unasserted. Added `assertDurationMetric` calls after each trace assertion, passing `DB_NAMESPACE` alongside `DB_SYSTEM_NAME`, `DB_OPERATION_NAME`, `SERVER_ADDRESS`, and `SERVER_PORT`. This matches the key set the instrumentation actually emits on metric points and follows the pattern used by the Jedis instrumentation tests.

Upsides: A regression that drops `db.namespace` from metric attributes is now caught by the test suite rather than silently passing.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: I think it is fine. On mysql someone could execute `use anotherdb`. Tracking whether or how databases allows changing this is too hard.
